test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Go the extra mile

options.text: Going in search of something better
Going above and beyond whatever is required for the task at hand

solution:
The correct answer is: **"Going above and beyond whatever is required for the task at hand."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given options, **"Going above and beyond whatever is required for the task at hand"** is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
 
• We use the idiom **"Go extra mile"** to mean "to do more than one is required to do".
 
 
• **Example:** She's always willing **to go the extra mile** to help a friend.
 
 
 
• Thus, ***option 3)*** is the correct alternative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let us see few more idioms related to the word - mile:

 
• **A mile a minute:** At a rapid pace.

 
 
• **Example:** She was walking a mile a minute to the school due to the fear of getting late.
 
 
 
• **Stick out a mile:** To be very conspicuous.
 
 
• **Example: **His lack of confidence stick out him a mile.
 
 
 
• **A mile off:** To notice very easily and quickly.
 
 
• **Example: **The employee was lying, one can tell it a mile off.
